last.verdict: Moderna swung to a profit on strong overseas COVID sales and lower R&D spending, but its jump in cash is mostly borrowed money.

takeaways.label: Profit and higher outlook
takeaways.text: Third-quarter revenue rose 29% to $1.3 billion, mainly from international COVID deliveries, and net income was $162 million versus a $200 million loss. Full-year revenue growth is now seen at 15%–25%, up from up to 10%.

takeaways.label: Cash boosted by debt
takeaways.text: Year-end cash is now seen at $8.1–$8.3 billion, up from $4.7–$5.2 billion, largely thanks to about $2.6 billion net from convertible notes. Most Q3 sales were still uncollected.

takeaways.label: Melanoma drug shows promise
takeaways.text: With Merck, Moderna's intismeran cut the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% when added to Keytruda in a Phase 3 trial. Regulatory filings are being prepared.

takeaways.label: Flu launch limited
takeaways.text: The U.S. approved mFLUSIVA for adults 50 and older, but approval came after contracting season ended, so this year's launch is limited. The norovirus vaccine's path forward is unclear.

history.verdict: Norovirus vaccine setback outweighed a smaller-than-expected loss and lower costs.

reasons.label: Norovirus vaccine setback
reasons.text: Phase 3 norovirus vaccine missed early-success bar; more patients must be enrolled, delaying it.

reasons.label: Pipeline over numbers
reasons.text: Revenue is only $145M, so the stock trades on upcoming flu and melanoma news.

reasons.label: Cost cuts, cash runway
reasons.text: Spending outlook trimmed about $0.2B; year-end cash now seen at $4.7–5.2B.
